demand.note: The hypothesis was partly wrong: there is no default value for the default instance warmup; it is off by default. Without it, instance refresh falls back to the grace period and target tracking / step scaling fall back to the default cooldown.
Hypothesis '300 seconds' holds only for the console. The page says the default is 0 seconds when the group is created with the AWS CLI or an SDK.
Facts from the earlier behavior/numbers runs; 48 hours is the global timeout (or 100 times the heartbeat timeout, whichever is smaller), the heartbeat range is 30 to 7200 seconds.

The scaling-plans FAQ fact aws-auto-scaling-faq-predictive-forecast-horizon says 'Every 24 hours' (scaling plans); the EC2 Auto Scaling guide says the forecast is updated every 6 hours. Different features; writers must not mix them.
Hibernation limits already live in the ec2 namespace (chapter 15); not duplicated here. The prerequisites page says Windows RAM must be less than or equal to 16 GiB and Linux RAM less than 150 GiB.
No page states what the API returns when desired capacity is set outside min and max; only the console behaviour (max raised) is documented on the manual scaling page.

source_notes: ec2-auto-scaling-scaling-cooldowns contradicts itself: its Considerations list says the group waits for terminating instances to deregister before starting the cooldown, while the lifecycle-hook section says that for scale in the cooldown starts when connection draining starts and does not wait for it. Recorded in the note of ec2-auto-scaling-cooldown-scale-in-starts-at-draining.

Conflicts queued by M12 (cf-0179 to cf-0184) pair quota or default rows that share wording but have different scopes (for example min versus max healthy percentage, per-call API limits versus per-group quotas); a registrar can close them with --both. The resume run queued cf-0211 to cf-0231 the same way: they pair the per-call array-member rows (attach versus detach, instances versus load balancers versus target groups), which have different scopes and do not contradict each other.
